🇲🇽💵 <u>SUPERPESO RALLIES: DOLLAR CLOSES AT 17.04, STRONGEST IN 2 YEARS</u>

Three straight days of gains: the Mexican peso closed at 17.04 per dollar on Thursday, its strongest level in over two years, El Financiero reports. With Banxico holding at 6.50% and July inflation at 3.12% — the lowest for that month in a decade — the currency keeps defying every collapse prophecy. The same analysts who swore the 4T would destroy the peso now watch it flirt with breaking below 17.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>ICE TO ARM AGENTS WITH ELECTRIC-SHOCK GLOVES IN $20M CONTRACT</u>

The agency hunting Mexican migrants across the US is getting new hardware: border czar Tom Homan publicly defended ICE's purchase of electric-shock gloves — a $20 million contract for thousands of "less lethal" devices already tested in US prisons. "It's another device to help someone comply when they're not doing so," Homan said. Human rights groups call the plan excessive and dangerous — this for an agency under fire after at least six civilians were shot dead by immigration agents and a string of deaths in custody.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>INEGI: NATIONAL GUARD DETENTIONS UP 137%, GUN SEIZURES UP 72%</u>

The security data the doom-mongers skip: INEGI's 2026 public security censuses show Mexico's National Guard nearly tripled its detentions in 2025 — up 137.4%, from 9,777 to 23,206 — while firearm seizures nationwide jumped 72.4% to 21,088 weapons. In total, police brought 413,127 people before authorities, 4% more than in 2024, including 66,968 for drug dealing. More capability, more seizures, more arrests — Mexico's security strategy shows up in the numbers, not the headlines.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>US REVOKES VISA OF AMLO'S SON — "HITLER-STYLE," HE FIRES BACK AT TRUMP</u>

The Trump administration revoked the US visa of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán — son of former president AMLO and a national Morena organizer. No charges, no evidence, pure political retaliation. In an open letter to Trump, López Beltrán called the move "politicking and propagandistic, Hitler-style," and asked the question Washington won't answer: if there's no motive beyond a "sick conservative phobia against Morena," why not fire Rubio and Landau, who act "like gang bosses, not statesmen"?

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SCIENTISTS WARN: MEXICO'S "WORLD-FIRST" RNA BIOFUNGICIDE ISN'T SAFE</u>

Mexico's Economy and Health secretaries announced with fanfare the world's first RNA biofungicide — developed by US firm Green Light Biosciences and fast-tracked by Cofepris even faster than in the US itself. Scientists consulted by Contralínea are sounding the alarm: "There is no scientific certainty, no consensus, and there is evidence of risk of grave or irreversible harm to the environment and human health — the State is obliged to apply the precautionary principle," said biologist Erica Hagman. Her verdict: "They're using us as an experimental field to grow their business."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>PENTAGON PLANS "LAND STRIKES" ON LATAM CARTELS — MEXICO NAMED</u>

Mexico just got its most explicit threat yet from Washington: US War Secretary Pete Hegseth said the Pentagon plans to attack drug traffickers "on land" in Latin America, vowing to eradicate them "from cocaine trafficking to fentanyl in the plazas of Mexico." President Sheinbaum's position hasn't moved: coordination, yes — subordination and foreign boots on Mexican soil, never. The same Pentagon whose boat strikes have killed at least 215 people in the Caribbean and Pacific now wants to bring that campaign ashore.

🇲🇽💻 <u>KIO DATA CENTERS BETS UP TO $1.3 BILLION ON MEXICO'S AI BOOM</u>

El Economista reports that Mexico's KIO Data Centers completed phases two and three of its QRO2 mega campus in Querétaro — $170 million invested — with another $200 million coming this year for CDMX, Monterrey and Querétaro. Next: up to $1.3 billion by 2030 for QRO3, a 100 MW facility that would be the largest data center in company history, plus 8,100 jobs. Marcelo Ebrard handed KIO the "Hecho en México" seal: the AI ecosystem "is going to be the new major economic growth, and Mexico is going to be part of it."

🇲🇽🎓 <u>1,437 WOMEN GRADUATE FROM CDMX'S ECONOMIC AUTONOMY PROGRAM</u>

Mexico City's Secretariat of Women graduated the first generation of its Women's Economic Autonomy Program: 1,437 participants with Ceneval-certified diplomas after two months of training in administration, digital marketing, leadership and personal finance — tools to launch their own projects or enter formal work. Under Clara Brugada the pilot became permanent policy. Coordinator María Elena Esparza: "That's what economic autonomy is about: the final goal is freedom."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>NAHLE TAKES SAN PEDRO SUGAR MILL'S FUTURE TO THE FEDERAL TABLE</u>

More than 6,000 families in Lerdo de Tejada, Veracruz depend on the San Pedro sugar mill — one of the complexes auctioned off under Vicente Fox. Governor Rocío Nahle is sitting down with Grupo Porres, the Economy Ministry and the SHCP to keep it alive, tying the rescue to the 4T's guaranteed-price policy for sugarcane. Her formula: "Dialogue, proposals, support — look everywhere."
banner: SUGAR: NAHLE FIGHTS TO SAVE SAN PEDRO MILL
